source.title: How benign is benign overfitting?
source.authors: Amartya Sanyal; P. Dokania; Varun Kanade; P. Torr

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training-error results under label noise, using toy-MNIST and full MNIST experiments to examine whether networks fit noisy labels.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses cited prior work on memorization and interpolation; those cited results are not extracted as rows. Figure 3 values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CNN training accuracy with randomized MNIST labels and compares natural with adversarial training. These test V1 in a new dataset setting. Its fully connected toy networks do not match V1's convolutional systems.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: fitting noisy labels can substantially damage adversarial robustness despite good natural generalization; robust training leaves some noisy and rare examples unfitted. The authors also emphasize that removing label noise alone is insufficient and that learned representations and invariances affect robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD training with noisy labels and reports training error, but experiments are on toy-MNIST and MNIST rather than the version's CIFAR benchmarks; initialization is not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: Toy-MNIST training error varied with sample variance; training errors on noisy labels differed between natural and adversarial training.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected toy-MNIST networks retain high training error at low sample variance but fit noisy labels perfectly at higher variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation of noisy labels in fully connected networks depends on input variability and distinguishability.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical results and experiments associate fitting label noise with increased adversarial vulnerability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing noisy labels can impair adversarial robustness even when natural test accuracy remains high.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), as stated in the supplied text
record.problems: Toy-MNIST training-error values are presented in a figure without recoverable numbers in the supplied text. The full-MNIST randomized-label comparison reports a single result without uncertainty or a stated seed count; model initialization is not stated.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100 interpolation; controlled CIFAR-10 random-label experiments; fully random labels; model-size dependence; SGD versus Adam; random-initialization dependence. Early-stopping evidence is confined to fully connected toy networks.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and extra-neuron interventions.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training deep plain or normalization-free residual networks.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Batch-normalization interventions, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

missing.what: Separate ResNet-50 training-accuracy rows for natural training and L2 adversarial training: epsilon 0, 0.25, and 1.0 yield 99.98%, 97.23%, and 86.03%. Verify dataset attribution; the table caption itself does not name it.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Selected-example errors in R5 can coexist with near-zero aggregate training error and therefore do not independently challenge V1. The supplied text does not establish this study's ICLR publication status; cited papers' venues are insufficient.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100; CIFAR-10 random-label training error; comparisons among SGD and Adam; model-size sweeps; corrupted labels beyond the reported MNIST setup; initialization details.
